judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]bserve all corporate formalities as a distinct entity" is unspecific, and both Borrowers are limited liability companies for which "corporate formalities" is an ill-fitting concept.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one limb of the Section 6.12 separateness package; the Board of Directors definition softens the corporate framing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence conflates two subjects — it requires the Borrower's "Books" to be separate and "otherwise readily identifiable as its own assets", so the referent of "its own assets" is broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with clause (d) and Section 6.1 the intent is discernible, but the text as written does not say what it means.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition on maintaining any depository account is subject to a nest of carve-outs ("except as herein specifically otherwise provided", "except for the Cash Management Accounts or as required by any written agreement between Fund and an Account Debtor"), which makes the scope hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.8 requires Administrative Borrower to maintain the Designated Account, Section 6.17 requires escrow deposits into a Deposit Account, and Section 5.18 contemplates a schedule of Deposit Accounts — all accounts this clause appears to forbid.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated environmental obligations with specific notice periods; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.14's representations and the Environmental Lien and Remedial Action definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A five-Business-Day notice obligation with an express anti-cure sentence; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly denies any amending effect on the Schedules, which sits against several representations that refer to schedules "as updated from time to time" — a small tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An empty placeholder; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) makes failure to observe "Section 6.15" an immediate Event of Default even though the section is intentionally omitted, so the default catalogue references a provision with no content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is expressly limited to what is "necessary to comply with Section 4.2", yet then imposes an unlimited obligation to deliver "all original promissory notes"; the two halves of the sentence pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 requires only $250,000,000 of Eligible Notes Receivable to be held, and Section 4.9(c) contemplates that assignments will have been recorded only in some cases; the delivery scope differs across these provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat covenant with an "including, without limitation" list; the general obligation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly reaches "funds delivered to any Borrower to be held on behalf of any Account Debtor", which Section 2.6(e) expressly excludes from the Escrow Account regime and Section 6.12(d) treats as a permitted exception — a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires escrow instructions demanding "each of the documents listed in Section 3.3(z)" — there is no clause (z) in Section 3.3, which stops at (f).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The document list the clause evidently intends is in Section 3.1(t), and a parallel but different list appears in the Eligible Notes Receivable definition clause (r); the cross-reference simply does not land.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard negative-covenant chapeau; the duration formula is compound but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6's chapeau states the covenant period differently ("so long as any credit hereunder shall be available and until payment in full"), so affirmative and negative covenants have textually different lives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of permitted Indebtedness, but the final item is lettered "(z)" rather than (g), and clause (f) permits refinancing only of clause (b) debt while imposing five detailed conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clauses (d) and (e) permit Subordinated Debt and Approved Debt, whose definitions conflict on whether such debt may be secured; Section 7.2 and Permitted Liens must then be read alongside.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad prohibition with a carefully bounded replacement-Lien parenthetical; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Lien definition sweeps in easements, leases and title exceptions, so the covenant is far broader than it looks and depends heavily on Permitted Liens clause (k) and clause (c)'s garbled Approved Debt proviso.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short prohibition with a single exception; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Permitted Reorganization exception permits admitting Manager and Servicer as members or managers, which can trigger the Change of Control prohibited by Section 7.8 without any reconciliation between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Repetitive but clear; the Permitted Reorganization carve-out is stated twice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.12's existence covenant and the Permitted Reorganization definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ll or any substantial part of its assets" uses an imprecise threshold that the immediately following Section 7.4 does not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.4 bars disposing of *any* assets other than Permitted Dispositions, which makes this "substantial part" limitation entirely redundant — two provisions covering the same ground at different thresholds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An absolute prohibition subject only to Permitted Dispositions; the words are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and overrides Section 7.3(c)'s narrower "substantial part" test, and its literal breadth must be squared with Permitted Investments clause (d), which contemplates ordinary-course lending.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise prohibition with a 30-day notice proviso; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.7(a)-(c) and 4.4(a)'s filing authorisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-outs permit "the curtailment in the origination of new loans" and suspension of new Investor Membership Interest offerings — i.e. the cessation of the very business the facility funds — while the covenant otherwise bars material changes; the boundary is genuinely obscure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.14(b)(i) contemplates using proceeds "to make new loans evidenced by an Eligible Note Receivable" and the Borrowing Base depends on eligible notes, so a permitted curtailment undercuts the facility's premise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated prohibitions with an opening exception; the phrase "in any manner that would be adverse to any Borrower" in clause (c) is oddly directed (it protects Borrower, not Lender).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to Sections 7.1(f) and 7.10 and to the applicable Subordination Agreement, which are the right cross-references; Section 8.10 makes an impermissible payment a default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line prohibition keyed to a defined term; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Permitted Reorganization definition expressly contemplates changes in Fund's membership and management that fall within the Change of Control definition, and Sections 7.3 and 7.6 carve out Permitted Reorganizations while this section does not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars changes "in any material respect" without "advance notice to, and consent by, the Lender", leaving both the materiality threshold and the form of consent unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower's Required Procedures definition requires Lender's prior *written* approval, in its *sole discretion*, for *any* amendment — a materially stricter rule than this covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permission for distributions "to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents" is open-ended, and the cross-reference to "Section 6.30b)" is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Restricted Payments definition is itself partly circular (clauses (d) and (e) turn on whether an Event of Default would occur or the payment is "expressly authorized in this Agreement"), so the prohibition and its definition chase each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A compound covenant, but each limb is specific and the GAAP carve-out is express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2, the GAAP definition and Section 6.3's cooperation provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short prohibition with two exceptions; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Investments clause (d) preserves ordinary-course lending and clause (f) Real Estate Owned, so the covenant does not stop the core business; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence bars forming or acquiring any Subsidiary, then the second sentence starts a lettered list under a different exception; the structure makes it unclear whether the Permitted Dispositions/Investments exception reaches the first sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subsidiary definition excludes most entities formed after the Closing Date, so a Borrower could form a new entity without breaching this covenant at all — the covenant and the definition largely cancel each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b)(ii) permits use "for working capital and general corporate needs", including funding obligations on Investor Membership Interests — a very wide permission inside a restrictive covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That breadth sits against Section 2.1(c)'s unfunded-commitment limit and against Section 7.10's restrictions on payments to members; the provisions are not obviously harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat bar with a specific proviso for loan files; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates verbatim the proviso in Section 5.5's representation, and works with Section 4.4(d)'s assignment of storage access rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dollar covenant tested monthly; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Tangible Net Worth definition adds Subordinated Debt to equity, and the $600,000,000 floor combined with Section 7.16(b)'s 0.9% ratio cap would confine Obligations to roughly $5.4 million against a $50,000,000 facility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A] Senior Leverage Ratio (expressed as a percentage) that is of no greater than nine-tenths of one percent (0.9%)" is both ungrammatical and, on its face, a wrong figure — a ratio of 0.9 (i.e. 90%) was plainly intended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As written the covenant is irreconcilable with the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount, the 20% Borrowing Base and the $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor: the borrower would breach the covenant on drawing about a tenth of the facility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 25% monthly test, though the numeral is rendered "twenty-live percent".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates the Defaulted Note Receivable definition, which turns on whatever Administrative Borrower or Lender "deems" non-performing, so a hard-edged covenant rests on a subjective input.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A payment default with no grace period, defined by reference to the Obligations; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Obligations definition includes "covenants" and "duties", so a literal reading of "fail to pay ... all or any portion of the Obligations" is broader than intended; otherwise consistent with Section 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause allocates cure periods by listing section numbers, an approach that fails if the numbering is wrong; limb (a) gives no cure at all for all of Section 7.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lists Section 6.15, which is "[Intentionally Omitted]", omits Section 6.4 (also blank), and lists Section 6.5 which the body mis-numbers "6.3" — the catalogue and the covenants do not line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]omes into the possession of any third Person" is extraordinarily broad and, read literally, is triggered by ordinary custodial arrangements; "material portion" is also unquantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 requires Notes Receivable to be held by "a custodian designated by Lender" — a third Person in possession of a material portion of the assets — so the default as written captures the transaction's own structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is numbered "3.4" and ends with a colon although nothing follows, leaving the sentence formally incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1's final paragraph refers to "any Event of Default described in Section 8.4 or Section 8.5", so the mis-numbering here matters to the automatic acceleration provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five enumerated triggers with a 45-day dismissal period; the internal provisos suspending credit are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is cross-referenced by Section 9.1's automatic acceleration paragraph, though numbered "3.5" in the text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n any way prevented by court order from continuing to conduct all or any material part of its business affairs" is broad but the trigger is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.3(c)'s parallel injunction condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[W]hether choate or otherwise" is an odd formulation, but the trigger (unpaid past delinquency) is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.7 and the Permitted Protest definition allow contested taxes, yet this default has no Permitted Protest carve-out — a real gap between covenant and default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dollar threshold with an objective trigger; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens clause (j) excepts judgment Liens "that [are] not an Event of Default hereunder", which points back to this section — circular but workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Material Adverse Change qualifier is attached only to limb (z), so defaults under limbs (x) and (y) trigger regardless of materiality, and limb (x) covers "capital obligations to any member or former member" — the fund's redemption obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (x) sits against the Permitted Reorganization definition, which contemplates withdrawing members being paid in Approved Debt, and against Section 7.10's restrictions on the very payments whose non-payment is a default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An objective trigger with an express carve-out for permitted payments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 7.7(b) and 7.10(b), which permit Subordinated Debt payments where the Subordination Agreement allows; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny material misstatement or misrepresentation" with no knowledge qualifier and no cure period is harsh but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5's chapeau already qualifies the representations "in all material respects", so materiality is applied twice; Section 6.14 says a later notice does not cure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The verb disagrees with the subject ("the obligations ... is terminated"), but the trigger is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Validity Agreements are Loan Documents required by Section 3.1(b)(iii) but are not in the record, so what termination "by operation of law" means depends on an absent instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It turns on an Executive Officer ceasing "to be employed in his current position with Manager or Servicer" although the Executive Officer definition attaches no positions to the five named individuals, and "his" does not fit one of them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Executive Officer, Authorized Person, Permitted Holder and Validity Agreement Party definitions each list overlapping but different individuals with different roles, and none identifies any office.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but precisely conditioned, with express carve-outs for permitted dispositions and permitted priority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.9(e)'s representation and the Permitted Liens definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line materiality-qualified default; the words are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Servicing Agreement is tripartite (Borrower, Servicer, Lender) but this default reaches only a Borrower's non-compliance, while Section 9.1(e)(ii) separately allows Lender to terminate that agreement — the default and the remedy are not aligned as to Servicer's own breach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Materiality is judged by what "Lender in its Permitted Discretion deems to be material", and the provision trails off with "or." as though an omitted limb followed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.17 follows, so the dangling "or" is a formatting artefact; substantively consistent with Sections 5.9(d) and 8.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise quantitative trigger with a three-Business-Day cure, qualified by "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It measures compliance by reference to Section 3.1(t), whose document list differs from the Eligible Notes Receivable clause (r) list and from Section 4.2's custodial requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A remedies chapeau with an express Code-compliance qualification plus a straightforward acceleration power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.6's automatic acceleration on termination and the final paragraph of Section 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cessation right; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.4, 8.5's provisos and Section 9.1's closing paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A termination right expressly preserving Liens and Obligations; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.6 sets out the effect of termination and Section 3.7(b) prices a Lender-elected termination after default, so three provisions govern the same event but consistently.
